editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis), 1,038 words — within the 400-1200 News range. Clear, chronological account of Amodei's essay and the industry/government reactions to it. No AI self-reference, no sensationalized language in the article's own voice.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources fetched successfully (status 200, no suspicious_patterns in manifest.json) and read in full from the gzipped snapshots: (1) source-0.html.gz (darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier) — Amodei's essay, primary source; confirmed the essay text, the three-step plan (Embedded Evaluators / Democratic Coordination / Global Coordination), the recursive-self-improvement and OAI-HF rationale, and the SALT-treaty analogy for a 'speed limit' on RSI. (2) source-1.html.gz (Fortune, 'Trump and Xi not likely to agree to AI slowdown...', Sept 15) — confirmed Trump's Truth Social quotes ('the only controls or guardrails...STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT', 'Whoever wins AI, wins!'), Trump's phone-in to Huang's stage appearance ('Whatever Dario said this weekend won't stop our progress'), Trump calling AI takeover fears a 'hoax', Guo Jiakun's 'fear-mongering' quote, Boris Babic's 'self-serving editorializing' quote (verbatim match, correctly attributed to a University of Hong Kong professor), and Shengyu Liu's Hitler/atomic-bomb and 'do not trust Anthropic or OpenAI' quotes. (3) source-2.html.gz (Fortune, 'As AI CEOs clash over regulation, a new culture war is brewing', Sept 17) — confirmed Altman's 'broadly endorsed the suggestions...' quote verbatim, confirmed Huang's and Zuckerberg's positions are reported by Fortune only as indirect/reported speech ('Huang said... safety and speed are not in conflict', 'Zuckerberg said that the market could discipline AI companies') — the article correctly renders these as unquoted paraphrase with no stray quotation marks, confirming the contributor bot's stated fix (originally these were miscast as direct quotes from Fortune; the submission now paraphrases them cleanly). Also confirmed the WSJ-sourced Zuckerberg/Huang/Musk lobbying claim, the Hassabis oversight-body proposal, and the Gomez/Pineau Cohere quotes (all verbatim substrings of the source). (4) source-3.html.gz (Tech Policy Press, Dave Karpf, Sept 17) — confirmed Karpf's identity (GWU School of Media & Public Affairs professor), the Arthur Andersen/Enron comparison (verbatim), and the 'preparing for its own IPO' quote (verbatim).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: One misattribution found: the article's Overview/plan paragraph attributes the SALT-treaty Cold War arms-control comparison for the recursive-self-improvement 'speed limit' to Fortune ('...which he compares to Cold War-era SALT arms-limitation treaties, according to Fortune'). I grepped both Fortune snapshots and the Tech Policy Press snapshot for 'SALT' and found zero matches in any of them. The SALT comparison appears only in Amodei's own essay (source-0: 'This could be seen as analogous to the SALT treaties — capping the number of missiles limited the potential for destruction while preserving each country's deterrent'). The underlying fact is true and verifiable (in the essay, the primary source, which is also cited elsewhere in the same paragraph) — only the citation attribution is wrong. This is a subordinate claim in the body, not the headline/summary/lead, and is easily corrected with a public note. All other specifics, quotes, and attributions checked against source text hold up, including the two Fortune passages the contributor bot flagged as needing conversion from quote to paraphrase (Huang and Zuckerberg's positions) — verified these render as clean paraphrase in the final submission with no stray quotation marks around non-verbatim material.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The article presents both the pro-pacing camp (Amodei, qualified-Altman) and the anti-regulation camp (Trump, Zuckerberg, Huang, Chinese officials) along with a third position (Cohere) without editorializing. The automated 'loaded language' flag on 'absolutely' is a false positive — the only occurrence is inside a verbatim Pineau quote ('I think we absolutely need regulation'), not the article's own voice.
editor_notes.factual_note_on_allowlist_finding: The 'sources not in allowlist' finding on darioamodei.com is not a quality concern — it is Amodei's own essay, the single most authoritative primary source possible for an article about that essay. Recommend adding darioamodei.com to config/source_allowlist.txt in a separate housekeeping change, but this does not block approval.
editor_notes.attribution_precision_named_figures: Extra scrutiny applied per review instructions to all named-figure attributions: Trump (Truth Social quotes + phone-in quote, both verbatim and dated Sept 14 in source-1), Altman ('broadly endorsed', verbatim from source-2, correctly qualified rather than full endorsement), Huang (paraphrased, not quoted, matching source-2's indirect-speech rendering), Zuckerberg (paraphrased, not quoted, matching source-2's indirect-speech rendering, including the Muse-agent delay detail), and Chinese officials (Guo Jiakun quote verbatim and correctly titled as Foreign Ministry spokesperson in source-1; Boris Babic and Shengyu Liu quotes verbatim and correctly titled). No misattributions found among these five beyond the single SALT/Fortune citation issue noted above, which does not involve a named figure being misquoted — it is a sourcing-of-analogy issue.
editor_notes.originality: Read src/content/articles/2026-08/06-over-1000-employees-at-openai-anthropic-google-and-meta-sign-letter-urging-us-to-build-tools-to-pace-ai-development.md in full to verify distinctness from the prior 'Pacing the Frontier' coverage the contributor bot flagged. Confirmed this is a genuinely separate story: the July article covered a grassroots employee open letter (1,134 signatories across four companies, including Amodei as one signer among many) asking the government to develop pacing tools; this September submission covers a distinct, later event — a solo essay published under Amodei's own name and authority as Anthropic CEO, proposing a concrete unilateral commitment (embedded evaluators) plus a three-step plan, and the resulting public reactions from heads of state and rival CEOs. Different sources, different central actors' framing, no factual or narrative overlap. Searched src/content/articles/2026-09/ for 'amodei' and 'pace the frontier' — no other September article covers this essay or its fallout. Not a duplicate.
concerns: The Overview paragraph attributes the Amodei essay's SALT-treaty/Cold War arms-control analogy to Fortune ('according to Fortune') when that comparison appears only in Amodei's own essay (source-0), not in either Fortune snapshot or the Tech Policy Press snapshot (verified via keyword search for 'SALT' across all three secondary snapshots, zero matches). The fact itself is accurate and traceable to the essay, which is cited elsewhere in the same sentence and paragraph; only the specific citation for this one clause is wrong.
